title: 第11章 想要册封的唐第12章 名望与魔法
slug: 骑士先生魔王真的不存在啊
lines: 第11章想要册封的唐
“这就是你说的要带我来的地方？”
看着正前方的高大建筑，再看四周神情状态比较放松的骑士护卫们，姆莉转头神情复杂地看向了唐。
“不错，镇长的办公城堡。”唐认真严肃地点头道。
姆莉闻言，嘴角不受控的开始抽搐，笑容也变得有些牵强。
还以为是什么好地方呢，故事里的男女主人公不都会在这种时候带着对方去旷野山坡上看流星什么的吗？都是假的……
姆莉心中叹气，传说故事的主人公待遇估计与她是彻底无缘了。
“那么，唐，我们来这里做什么？”姆莉拿出了纸笔，准备记录下唐的回答。
“讨要册封。”
听到唐的回答，姆莉手中的木笔差点一滑，马上向他投来诧异的目光。
“向镇长讨要册封吗？”姆莉神情怪异，考虑到唐的脑子有问题，好像一切又能说得通。
可镇长哪里是唐说见就能见的？人家多多少少也是一个贵族吧？哪怕这个爵位不高，但对于平民而言也是一片天呐。
“没错，我们这次解决了困扰了骑士团一月有余的案件，救回了不少人，依律应是能够讨要册封骑士身份的。”唐说明了情况。
听到这里，姆莉算是明白唐为何会插手骑士团的事情了，原来是为了册封啊。
回忆着亚里罗王国的律法，姆莉竟觉得真有可行性，于是就跟着唐走向了城主的城堡。
见到二人靠近，马上就有几位骑士过来挡住了他们。
“几位留步，这里是镇长的城堡，若无要事就请你们离开。”一位骑士紧紧盯着唐，似乎还有些不耐烦。
“唐，你又是来要册封的吗？镇长不会同意的，你回去吧。”另一位骑士对唐劝说道。
姆莉闻言，意外地瞥了唐一眼。原来唐不是第一次来讨要骑士册封了呀。
“依据律法，我救回了大量群众，为骑士团提供了关键助力，应当可以册封骑士。”唐认真道。
“唐，小地方的话语权就在贵族手上，镇长的话就是律法。”前一位骑士带着不耐烦的语气说。
“贵族身份是律法赋予的，若贵族凌驾于律法之上，身份便失效了，那他便不是贵族，不受律法约束者不受律法保护。”唐压低了眉毛，更严肃了。
听他说出如此大逆不道的话，姆莉有些心急，可仔细一想，唐的话竟是那么的有道理。
她明明是第一次听到这样的言论，可为何会如此信服呢？姆莉为此困惑，但她大抵会站在唐这边。
那位不耐烦的骑士一声咋舌，想要动手将唐赶走，但另一位骑士却拦住了他，摇着脑袋说：“让他们进去，镇长会说服他的。”
于是二人就在这位骑士的带领下进入了城堡，并以“有两位立了功劳的平民想要面见镇长”为由通报。
“镇长，人就在外面。”
在政务厅外等候，唐与姆莉可以听到骑士的通报声，以及镇长怨气极重的声音。
“让他们进来吧。”
姆莉能够听出镇长语气中压抑着愤怒，于是转头看向身旁神态平静的唐，鼓起勇气跟在他的身后，一同进入了厅内。
“勇敢的……唐？”镇长公式化的开场白在认清来人是唐后立刻收了起来。

Chapter 11 Tang who wants to be canonized
"Is this where you said you were going to take me?"
Looking at the tall building in front of her and the knight guards around her who were looking relatively relaxed, Mu Li turned to look at Tang with a complicated expression.
"Yes, the mayor's office castle." Tang nodded seriously.
When Mu Li heard this, the corners of her mouth began to twitch uncontrollably, and her smile became a little forced.
I thought it was a good place. Wouldn’t the hero and heroine in the story always take each other to the wilderness to watch shooting stars on the hillside at times like this? It's all fake...
Mu Li sighed in her heart. The treatment of the protagonist of the legendary story was probably completely out of reach for her.
"So, Tang, what are we doing here?" Muli took out a pen and paper, preparing to record Tang's answer.
"Ask for canonization."
Hearing Tang's answer, the wooden pen in Mu Li's hand almost slipped and she immediately cast a surprised look at him.
"Are you going to ask the mayor for a canonization?" Muli looked strange. Considering that there was something wrong with Tang's brain, everything seemed to make sense.
But where could the mayor be seen by Tang as soon as he saw him? He is more or less a noble, right? Even if this title is not high, it is still a blessing for common people.
"Yes, we have solved the case that has troubled the Knights for more than a month this time and rescued many people. Yilu should be able to ask for the knighthood." Tang explained the situation.
After hearing this, Mu Li finally understood why Tang would intervene in the Knights' affairs. It turned out to be for canonization.
Recalling the laws of the Kingdom of Arilo, Muli felt that it was really feasible, so she followed Tang to the castle of the city lord.
Seeing the two approaching, several knights immediately came over to block them.
"Stay here, everyone. This is the mayor's castle. If you have nothing important to do, please leave." A knight stared at Tang closely, seeming a little impatient.
"Tang, are you here to ask for canonization again? The mayor will not agree. You can go back." Another knight advised Tang.
Hearing this, Mu Li glanced at Tang unexpectedly. It turns out that this is not the first time Tang has come to ask for knighthood.
"According to the law, I rescued a large number of people and provided key support to the Knights. I should be able to be canonized as a knight." Tang said seriously.
"Don, the nobles have the right to speak in small places, and the mayor's words are the law." The previous knight said with an impatient tone.
"Noble status is given by law. If a noble is above the law, the status will be invalid. Then he is not a noble. Those who are not bound by the law are not protected by the law." Tang lowered his eyebrows and became more serious.
Hearing him say such treacherous words, Muli was a little anxious, but when she thought about it carefully, Tang's words turned out to be so reasonable.
It was obviously the first time she heard such remarks, but why was she so convinced? Mli is confused by this, but she will probably side with Don.
The impatient knight gasped and wanted to drive Tang away, but another knight stopped him, shook his head and said: "Let them go in, the mayor will convince him."
So the two of them entered the castle under the leadership of the knight, and reported that "two civilians who have made meritorious services want to meet the mayor."
"Mayor, the person is outside."
Waiting outside the Government Affairs Hall, Tang and Muli could hear the knight's announcement and the mayor's resentful voice.
"Let them in."
Muli could hear the suppressed anger in the mayor's tone, so she turned to look at Tang, who was calm beside her, and mustered up the courage to follow him and enter the hall together.
"Brave... Tang?" The mayor's formulaic opening statement was immediately put away after he recognized that the person coming was Tang.
